turns.user: are direct flights from sfo to denver actually cheaper on tuesdays or is that just a myth lol

SFO to DEN has a lot of nonstops, so fares move with competition more than with the day. The better move is to check the date grid on Google Flights for your month, since it shows the cheapest days at a glance, and set a price alert for your exact dates.

turns.user: perfect. one more, is it better to book on the airline site or on google flights
turns.assistant: Book directly with the airline when you can. If something changes, the airline can rebook you without a middleman, and you deal with one support team. Use Google Flights to find the cheapest option, then check that same flight on the airline site before you pay.

turns.user: how do i get the full traceback into the log file when an exception happens inside a celery task. right now only the message is getting logged
i did that and it still only shows the message. the worker logs look normal otherwise
turns.assistant: Celery sets up its own root logger when the worker starts, which can replace the handler you configured. Turn that off in your config with app.conf.worker_hijack_root_logger = False. Then configure logging yourself with logging.config.dictConfig, or make sure your handler is attached to the logger you're using. If you start the worker with --logfile, try running without it and log to a file from your own config instead.

turns.user: i have 3 days a week at the gym and im kinda bored of full body. what are some other splits i could try. not looking for a full plan just ideas
turns.assistant:
A few options that work with three sessions a week:

- Upper / lower / upper: two upper days and one lower, so the upper body gets more volume.
- Push / pull / legs: each muscle group gets trained about every 1.5 weeks, and you alternate which day you start on.
- Strength-focused 3 day: heavy squats, deadlifts, bench and rows, with accessories added for weak points.
- Full body with a heavy and a light day: one day of heavy compound lifts, one of higher reps, one of machines and isolation work.

Push / pull / legs and upper / lower are the most popular for three days, so start there and see what feels good.

turns.user: the push pull legs one sounds fun but with 3 days wouldnt i miss legs every other week
turns.assistant: Yes, on a fixed Monday, Wednesday, Friday schedule, legs only get hit once a week, and that's fine for most people. If you want legs more often, rotate the order each week. Week one is push, pull, legs. Week two starts with legs, then push, then pull. That way no group always sits on the same days, and legs get some extra recovery time. If recovery is an issue, keep the second leg day a bit lighter.

turns.user: quick question, if i only pay the minimum on my card at 24% apr is it going to take forever to clear a 6000 balance
turns.assistant: Very long, usually. Most minimum payments are around 1% of the balance plus interest, so on 6000 at 24% the early payments are mostly interest, and the payment shrinks as the balance drops. Depending on the card's minimum formula, paying only the minimum commonly takes 20 to 30 years, and the interest can end up more than the original balance. Your statement or a payoff calculator with your exact APR and minimum rule will give you the real number.

turns.user: ok so if i put 300 a month instead, roughly how long
turns.assistant: At 24% APR that's about 2% interest per month. Interest on 6000 is about 120 in the first month, so 300 a month chips away at principal quickly. You'd be done in roughly 26 months, paying about 7,800 total, so around 1,800 of that is interest. Going from the minimum to 300 a month saves you many years and thousands of dollars.

turns.user: and if i do the 300 but also stop using the card, does that change anything
turns.assistant: The payoff math stays the same, but stopping new charges matters a lot. If you keep adding to the card while paying 300, the balance may fall slowly or not at all. If you can't fully stop, look at a 0% balance transfer card, which often gives 15 to 21 months with a 3 to 5% transfer fee. On 6000 with a 3% fee, that's 180 upfront and no interest while you pay it down, as long as you can clear the full amount before the promo ends.
